To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the kinematic number, defined as a product of rotation ratios of pad and wafter, and the ratio of wafer radius and pad radius, can be used to predict uniformity of velocity, direction of friction, and uniformity and distribution of sliding distance.

(1) the velocity distribution, direction and uniformity of the friction force, sliding distance and its uniformity can be expressed by a single kinematic parameter ζ, (2) the uniformity of the velocity distribution and sliding distance distribution is improved by increasing the kinematic number, and (3) the kinematic number is a key parameter for the uniformity of CMP results.
the kinematic number is a new parameter that can be used to predict CMP uniformity and that the kinematic-number concept can be used to optimize the design of the CMP system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the kinematics of conventional rotary CMP.
the effects of kinematic conditions of CMP on polishing uniformity, and it is shown that kinematic conditions can be expressed in terms of a single parameter, ζ.
the kinematics and dynamics of the CMP process and the effects of the kinematic parameters on the CMP process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the kinematic number, which is a measure of the relative size of the pad and wafer, determines the uniformity of velocity, direction of friction, uniformity of sliding, and uniformity in sliding distance.
ζ should be minimized to achieve uniform wear distance, which is the key to achieving uniformity of polishing results.
the uniformity of the velocity and sliding distance of pad and the direction of the friction force are the most important parameters for the CMP process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ζ is a key parameter for CMP process control.
the uniformity of the velocity distribution and the sliding distance distribution are the most important parameters in CMP.
the kinematic number is an important factor for the uniformity of polishing result in the CMP process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the uniformity of velocity, sliding distance, and friction force is a function of the kinematic numbers, and that these numbers should be kept constant for a given wafer size.
a CMP tool with a large kinematic number ζ will produce a uniform polishing result.
the uniformity of velocity is a key to uniformity of wear distance.
